one-sentence-definition: A cohesive boundary within a domain model where a single ubiquitous language applies (DDD).
A deliberately-defined subset of tenants grouped for rollout, billing, or routing decisions.
Mechanism for assigning infrastructure cost (compute, storage, network) to specific tenant identities.
A discontinuity between tiers (price jump, feature jump) that incentivizes user workarounds rather than upgrades.
The per-unit-of-business revenue, cost, and margin model; for SaaS the unit is typically a tenant or seat.
The mechanism for enabling/disabling features based on a tenant's tier, role, or other attribute.
GDPR Art 17 subject-erasure right; tenant or subject can request hard-delete of PII data subject to regulatory retention floors.
GDPR Art 20 right; tenant can request machine-readable structured export of their data before erasure or migration.
Regulatory minimum retention window (HIPAA 6y, SOX 7y, PCI 1y) that constrains the timing of deletion or anonymization.
Irreversible removal or alteration of PII such that the original subject cannot be re-identified; distinct from pseudonymization which is reversible (latter deferred to PX-Glossary or P9 Trust wave).
Escape from row-level-security policies via SECURITY DEFINER functions, role-elevation, or function-call escalation; primary RLS-failure mode.
Tenant whose resource consumption degrades other tenants' SLAs; mitigated via quotas, fair-scheduling, and rate-limiting.
Mandatory onboarding step that verifies a newly-provisioned tenant cannot read or write to other tenants' data; blocking gate before live traffic.
